rules.quote: Alerts are defined as events that have security implications, and should be handled by the main processor, or escalated to other hardware modules to take action.
rules.statement: Alerts are events with security implications and must be handled by the main processor or escalated to other hardware modules for action.

rules.quote: Those peripherals should instantiate one module (prim_alert_sender) to convert the event associated with that alert into a signal to the alert handler module.
rules.condition: A peripheral defines an alert signal
rules.statement: Peripherals defining alerts must instantiate a prim_alert_sender to convert the alert event into a signal to the alert handler.

rules.quote: The differential signaling submodules may either use a synchronous or asynchronous clocking scheme, since the message type to be transferred is a single discrete event.
rules.statement: The differential signaling submodules may use either a synchronous or an asynchronous clocking scheme.

rules.quote: Alerts are encoded differentially and signaled using a full handshake on the alert_tx_i/o.alert_p/n and alert_rx_i/o.ack_p/n wires. The handshake pattern is repeated as long as the alert is true.
rules.statement: Alerts are differentially encoded and signaled with a full handshake on alert_p/n and ack_p/n, repeated as long as the alert is true.

rules.quote: The full handshake guarantees that alert messages are correctly back-pressured and no alert is "lost" at the asynchronous boundary due to (possibly variable) clock ratios greater or less than 1.0.
rules.statement: The full handshake must back-pressure alert messages correctly so no alert is lost at the asynchronous boundary regardless of clock ratio.

rules.quote: The "native alert message" will be repeated on the output wires as long as the alert event is still true within the peripheral.
rules.condition: Alert event is still true within the peripheral
rules.statement: The native alert message is repeated on the output wires as long as the alert event remains true.

rules.quote: The sender will wait for 2 cycles between handshakes.
rules.statement: The sender waits 2 cycles between handshakes.

rules.quote: Note that the alert is immediately propagated to alert_o once the initial level change on alert_tx_i.alert_p/n has been received and synchronized to the local clock on the receiver side. This ensures that the first occurrence of an alert is always propagated - even if the handshake lines have been manipulated to emulate backpressure.
rules.condition: Initial level change on alert_tx_i.alert_p/n received and synchronized, even if handshake lines are manipulated to emulate backpressure
rules.statement: The receiver must immediately propagate the first alert occurrence to alert_o after synchronizing the initial level change on alert_tx_i.alert_p/n.

rules.quote: The alert sender and receiver modules can either be used synchronously or asynchronously.
rules.statement: The alert sender and receiver modules can be used either synchronously or asynchronously.

rules.quote: The signaling protocol remains the same in both cases, but the additional synchronizer flops at the diff pair inputs may be omitted, which results in lower signaling latency.
rules.statement: The signaling protocol remains the same in both synchronous and asynchronous use; synchronizer flops at the diff pair inputs may be omitted.

rules.quote: All differential pairs are monitored for signal integrity issues, and if an encoding failure is detected, the receiver module asserts a signal integrity alert via integ_fail_o. The alert_tx_i.alert_p/n pair is not correctly encoded on the receiver side. This can be directly flagged as an integrity failure on the receiver side.
rules.condition: alert_tx_i.alert_p/n pair is not correctly encoded at the receiver
rules.statement: The receiver must assert integ_fail_o when alert_tx_i.alert_p/n is incorrectly encoded.

rules.quote: All differential pairs are monitored for signal integrity issues, and if an encoding failure is detected, the receiver module asserts a signal integrity alert via integ_fail_o. The alert_rx_i.ping_p/n or the alert_rx_i.ack_p/n pairs are not correctly encoded on the sender side. This is signaled to the receiver by setting the alert_tx_o.alert_p/n wires to the same value, and that value will be continuously toggled. This implicitly triggers a signal integrity alert on the receiver side.
rules.condition: ping_p/n or ack_p/n pair is not correctly encoded at the sender
rules.statement: The sender must set alert_tx_o.alert_p/n to the same continuously toggling value, causing the receiver to assert integ_fail_o.

rules.quote: Note that if signal integrity failures occur during ping or alert handshaking, it is possible that the protocol state-machines lock up and the alert sender and receiver modules become unresponsive. However, the above mechanisms ensure that this will always trigger either a signal integrity alert or eventually a "pingfail" alert.
rules.condition: Signal integrity failures occur during ping or alert handshaking and the protocol locks up
rules.statement: A protocol lock-up must always trigger either a signal integrity alert or eventually a pingfail alert.
